cards.explanation: The answer is an altar. God tells Jacob, “Build an altar there to the God who appeared to you when you fled from your brother Esau.” Esau is Jacob's brother. So the order is simple, friends: get up, go to Bethel, and build the altar. Nobody needs a blueprint for that one.

The answer is the foreign gods among them. Jacob tells his household and all who were with him, “Get rid of the foreign gods that are among you.” That comes before anything else on his list, friends. If you're headed to worship the one God, you drop the other gods at the door.

The answer is to change their garments. Jacob says, “Purify yourselves and change your garments.” Then he says they will go to Bethel, where he will build an altar to God. Whenever I put on a clean apron, I stand up a little straighter myself, friends.

The answer is earrings. The household hands Jacob “…all their foreign gods and all their earrings…” (Genesis 35:4). Picture him standing there with his arms getting fuller and fuller, friends. Then he buries the whole pile under the oak near Shechem, and they're ready to head for Bethel.

The answer is True. The text says, “…Jacob buried them under the oak near Shechem.” The word "them" is the foreign gods and the earrings the household had just handed over, friends. So both of them go under that oak.

The answer is terror. The text says, “…a terror from God fell over the surrounding cities…” It came from God Himself, and it fell on the cities around them. I think that was good news for Jacob's sons, friends.

The answer is False. The terror from God fell over the surrounding cities “…so that they did not pursue Jacob’s sons.” So the cities do not chase them, friends. The statement says they did, and that's why it's False.

The answer is El-bethel. The verse says, “There Jacob built an altar, and he called that place El-bethel…” That's the place Luz, which is also called Bethel, friends. Same ground, one more name for it.

The answer is that God revealed Himself to him there as he fled. The text says he named it El-bethel “…because it was there that God had revealed Himself to Jacob as he fled from his brother.” So the name remembers what God did at that spot, friends. Jacob's back where it happened.
The answer is Israel. God says, “Instead, your name will be Israel.” And then the verse adds, “So God named him Israel.” Jacob now has a new name straight from God, friends.

The answer is kings. God promises that a nation, even a company of nations, will come from Israel, and He says, “…and kings shall descend from you.” That's a big promise to give a man, friends. Kings are part of it.

The answer is Abraham. God says, “The land that I gave to Abraham and Isaac I will give to you…” Abraham is Isaac's father (Genesis 25:19). So God names both of them as the ones He gave the land to, friends, and says He will give it to Jacob and to his descendants after him.

The answer is a stone pillar. The text says, “…Jacob set up a pillar in the place where God had spoken with him…” and it calls it a stone marker. Then he pours a drink offering on it and anoints it with oil. I mark my spots with cookie stamps, friends, so a stone marker is a step up.

The answer is True. The text says Jacob “…poured out a drink offering on it and anointed it with oil.” The word "it" is the stone pillar he just set up where God had spoken with him, friends. So the drink offering goes on the pillar, and the oil follows.

The answer is that she is having another son. The midwife tells Rachel, “Do not be afraid, for you are having another son.” Rachel is in severe labor, friends, so those words land in a hard moment. I think this is a heavy part of the story.

The answer is Benjamin. The verse says Rachel named him Ben-oni, “But his father called him Benjamin.” So the boy ends up with the name his father gave him, friends. Verse 24 lists Joseph and Benjamin as Rachel's sons.
The answer is True. The verse says Rachel “…was buried on the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem).” So the text itself says those are the same place, friends. One road, two names.
The answer is False. After Reuben's sin, the verse says, “…and Israel heard about it.” Israel is Jacob's new name, friends. So the news did reach him.

The answer is his father Isaac. The verse says, “Jacob returned to his father Isaac at Mamre, near Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron), where Abraham and Isaac had stayed.” So Jacob comes back to his father Isaac at Mamre, friends. Hebron is the other name for Kiriath-arba.

The answer is Jacob and his brother Esau. The verse says, “And his sons Esau and Jacob buried him.” Both of Isaac's sons were there for it, friends. It's a quiet and heavy moment, and the two brothers stand together.
